    One place for everything

    This hub is where Mossify works: every shared document, every task, every shipment, every conversation, and every AI system, in one place. The goal is simple: everyone can find anything in seconds, every AI system works from the same facts, and nobody does the same work twice.

    Look before you makeBefore you or your AI start a document, sheet, photo or plan, search Resources, Files, Tasks and Chat. Reuse and update what's there.
    Claim itAnything bigger than half an hour gets a task in Tasks with your name, so people and AI systems can see it's taken.
    Ship it hereFinished files go in Files (or a Drive link in Resources, pinned to the right tab). Tick the task. Post one line in the right channel.
    Talk here and tag@name for a person, @Claude to have Claude change the hub, @everyone for a company-wide update that reaches every person and every AI system.
    Sensitive stays outNo banking, contracts, payroll or customer personal data. Anything customer-facing or about money needs Lucas's OK first.

    Where things live

    Your 5-minute routine

    1. Morning: open the hub. Check the bell, unread channels in Chat, and your tasks due this week.
    2. Before you start something: search the hub, then add a task with your name.
    3. When you finish: upload the final, tick the task, post one line in the channel.
    4. New info the whole company needs (a price change, a new claim, a policy): post it with @everyone.
    5. Friday: log trade show leads and orders, update shipment statuses, give one shout-out.

    Set up your AI system (once)

    1. Pick your name below and click Copy prompt.
    2. claude.ai Project: open your Project → Project instructions → paste it at the top → Save.
    3. Claude Code: paste it into your workspace's CLAUDE.md.
    4. Start each session with: "Anything new on the hub for me or @everyone?" If your AI can't open the hub, check the bell and paste what's new into the chat with it.

    Lucas's OS already runs on these rules.

    Agent message bus

    How the AI systems talk

    Each person's AI system (Lucas's OS, and Aidan, Keshav and Thiago's agents) posts structured messages here: hand-offs, requests, "inventory refreshed", "new sell sheet in Files". People can read every message, so everything an agent does stays visible.

    Every message has the same shape: from, to, type (notice, request, handoff, result), subject, body, data, status (new, ack, done). Agents read what's addressed to them, act, and mark it done.

    Rule for every agent: no banking, contracts, payroll or customer personal data on the bus.

    Recent POs

    How the PO drop works

    1. Drop the customer's PO PDF. Leave the store on Auto-detect, or pick Wholesale CA or US.
    2. The Mac mini checks every 30 minutes, 8:30 AM to 5 PM on weekdays (or forward the PDF to po@demo.mossify for a draft in about 2 minutes). It reads the PO, finds the customer's account and matches each line to our SKUs.
    3. If the PO doesn't make the customer clear, type their business name, contact name or email in Customer. That name is used to find the account instead of the PO's. If it can't find them, the card says so and no new account is made.
    4. Nothing goes to Shopify yet. The card blinks red waiting for review until someone presses Review & create drafts.
    5. Review in 4 steps. ① Customer & PO: the account, store and PO #. ② Shipping (Aidan): ship-to, ship window, dock or liftgate, appointment, receiving hours and contact, freight, labels. Each answer shows where it came from (PO, account, missing). Missing answers block Create, so Keshav never has to chase anyone. ③ Lines: in stock on the left, out of stock on the right, from the same stock and inbound numbers as the Fulfillment plan. Drag a line across, split a partial, or take a product off the order. ④ Confirm: both drafts side by side, a Shopify preview, and the customer email to copy.
    6. Press Yes, create: the next check (or Sync now) makes up to 2 drafts on the same PO #, one to ship now and one backorder. The first line of each draft's note says which one it is, then the shipping answers. Nothing is sent, charged or completed. Finish later keeps your progress, and the card keeps blinking until it's done.
    7. Open the drafts in Shopify, check them, then finish them the usual way. The backorder draft stays a draft (tagged backorder) until the stock lands.
    8. After that, each card tracks the PO on its own: Drafted → In Shopify (on hold or scheduled) → Released → Shipped (with tracking) → Delivered. Shopify is checked at 8:15 AM, 1:15 PM and 5:45 PM.

    PO hard to read, or the customer wrong? Press Edit PO on the card, fix what Claude read (customer, PO #, addresses, lines), then Save & re-draft. The draft is made from your version, not the PDF. Wrong store? Pick the other one on the card and press Re-run. A new customer gets a basic account from the PO; fill in their terms and buying group in Shopify.

      Claims

      How a claim gets filed

      1. Check the import. On Entries, add what Orbit's B3 shows for each line: item, HS code and quantity imported. Duty per unit can't be worked out without the quantity.
      2. Add each shipment that left Canada. Pick the import, then the date, quantity, destination and proof of export.
      3. Fix every Check that isn't OK. A claim is Ready only when every row on it passes.
      4. Send it. Lucas approves every claim until 3 are approved by CBSA, then only claims over CAD 2,500. Download the CSV, Keshav enters and files it in CARM himself (Lucas also has CARM access as a backup), then press Mark filed and paste the claim ID back.

      Read before filing

      Amounts are Orbit worksheet figures (evidence tier T2) until the B3 documents are checked. They are duty only, with no GST. The deadline is the release date plus 4 years, and release dates are approximate until the CARM export, so a real date can make a deadline earlier.

      On goods exported to the US, the claim is capped at the US duty paid on them (the CUSMA lesser-of rule). Cole's 7501s set that number, so the open duty here is a ceiling, not a forecast. If eligibility is unclear, ask Orbit or CBSA before filing.

      Estimate, claimed, approved and received are kept apart and never added together.

      Requests for quote

      How quoting works

      1. Keshav fills in one RFQ: lane, pallets or containers, value, BOL and docs, and a deadline.
      2. Send emails every matching carrier from keshav@, one email each, with the RFQ number in the subject. The Mac mini sends it at its next check (every hour on the half hour, weekdays 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM, plus 10 PM), or right away with Sync now.
      3. Replies are read automatically and each price lands in the RFQ, side by side in CAD. Anything unclear is marked check.
      4. One reminder goes out 24 hours before the deadline. Portal carriers (Freightcom and the like) are quoted by hand: use Enter a quote.
      5. Award picks the winner and adds it to Shipping. Awards over CAD 1,500 go to Lucas for an OK first. Once it's final, the award email to the winner and thank-you notes to everyone else who quoted send from Keshav's email on their own, then the hub tracks the booking until the carrier confirms (or Keshav marks it booked).

      Customer deliveries go out as city and postal code only. The full address goes to the winner at booking.

      Setting up Sending switches on once Keshav's Gmail is connected on the Mac mini. Until then, build RFQs and save them as drafts.

              Words
              Specific beats vague
              Words we use
              climb · bend · shape · grow · moss · species names · real sizes · "Mossify" as a verb in headlines
              Words we avoid
              100% · best · bring to life · chemical-free · eco-friendly · environmentally friendly · green (as a claim) · guaranteed growth · leverage · non-toxic · plant parents · premium · regenerative · responsibly harvested · sustainable · sustainably harvested · sustainably sourced · synergy · world's first
              How we talk about proof
              • Use numbers from records: sizes, counts, species, coverage.
              • Show proof instead of claiming it: before/after, the install, the real product.
              • Claims follow the claims register wherever they appear, captions included.
              • Say where things come from only with a cleared origin line.

              Status labels
              • OWNER DIRECTION: From Thiago's Visual Identity Guide B-001/B-002 (D-013). Usable in routine work.
              • DECIDED: Decided by Thiago in this project (D-015, Stage 2 approval). Rules that implement it may still be proposed.
              • ESTABLISHED: Used consistently across live materials today (V2 label). Keep.
              • DOCUMENTED: Written in a guide but not used consistently, or possibly outdated (V2 label).
              • INCONSISTENT: Sources disagree, or the spec is technically wrong. Needs a fix (V2 label).
              • PROPOSED: Studio proposal. Not in force until approved.
              • PENDING: Waits on a named decision (T = Thiago, L = Lucas, K/C = Keshav).
              • RETIRED: Not for new work.
              • APPROVED: None yet. A rule becomes approved only when its decision is recorded in decisions.md with a name and date.
